{{Short description|German physicist}}

'''Karl Leo''' (born 10 July 1960 in [[Freiburg im Breisgau]], Baden-Württemberg, Germany) is a German physicist. He holds the chair of optoelectronics at the Dresden Integrated Center for Applied Physics and Photonic Materials (IAPP) of TU Dresden and is a leading researcher on organic semiconductors. He is known for the controlled electrical doping of organic thin films and the resulting highly efficient organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) and organic solar cells, and for the first experimental generation and detection of Bloch oscillations in a semiconductor superlattice. Leo has co-founded several technology spin-off companies based upon his research, among them Novaled<ref>{{Cite web |title=News &amp; Press |url=https://www.novaled.com/news-press/newsitem/press-release-novaled-iapp-and-technical-university-of-dresden-honoured/ |access-date=2026-07-20 |website=NOVALED {{!}} Creating the OLED Revolution |language=en-GB}}</ref> and Heliatek.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Spin-offs |url=https://tu-dresden.de/dcpc/iapp/erfolge/ausgruendungen?set_language=en |access-date=2026-07-20 |website=TU Dresden |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Karl Leo: Seltene Doppelbegabung - brand eins online |url=https://www.brandeins.de/magazine/brand-eins-wirtschaftsmagazin/2022/gross-denken/karl-leo-seltene-doppelbegabung |access-date=2026-07-20 |website=www.brandeins.de |language=de}}</ref> His honours include the [[Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize]] (2002),<ref>{{Cite web |title=DFG - Wissenschaftliche Preise |url=http://www.dfg.de/aktuelles_presse/preise/leibniz_preis/2002/leo/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070929083716/http://www.dfg.de/aktuelles_presse/preise/leibniz_preis/2002/leo/index.html |archive-date=2007-09-29 |access-date=2026-07-20 |website=www.dfg.de}}</ref> the [[Deutscher Zukunftspreis]] (2011),<ref>{{Cite news |title=Preisträger 2011 |url=https://www.deutscher-zukunftspreis.de/de/preistraeger-2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190824025713/https://www.deutscher-zukunftspreis.de/de/preistraeger-2011 |archive-date=2019-08-24 |access-date=2026-07-20 |work=Deutscher Zukunftspreis |language=de}}</ref> the [[:de:Blaise-Pascal-Medaille|Blaise Pascal Medal]] in Physics (2021)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Karl Leo receives Blaise Pascal Medal of the European Academy of Sciences |url=https://tu-dresden.de/mn/der-bereich/news/karl-leo-erhaelt-blaise-pascal-medaille-der-european-academy-of-sciences?set_language=en |access-date=2026-07-20 |website=TU Dresden |language=en}}</ref> and the [[Order of Merit of the Free State of Saxony|Order of Merit of the Free State of Saxony (2025)]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Mundus |first=Jana |title=Der Erfinder der Oleds: Forscher Karl Leo erhält Sachsens Verdienstorden |url=https://www.saechsische.de/wissen/regional/erfinder-der-oleds-karl-leo-von-der-tu-dresden-erhaelt-sachsens-verdienstorden-YOQ2SW7SJFCWTPBZCOJFOOCD7M.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250623105550/https://www.saechsische.de/wissen/regional/erfinder-der-oleds-karl-leo-von-der-tu-dresden-erhaelt-sachsens-verdienstorden-YOQ2SW7SJFCWTPBZCOJFOOCD7M.html |archive-date=2025-06-23 |access-date=2026-07-20 |work=SZ - Sächsische Zeitung |language=de-DE}}</ref> 

==Education and Career==
After his [[Abitur]] in 1979 in [[Sankt Georgen im Schwarzwald|St. Georgen im Schwarzwald]] and military service in 1980, Leo studied physics at the [[University of Freiburg|Albert-Ludwigs-Universität Freiburg]], graduating in 1985 with a diploma thesis on solar cells carried out at the [[Fraunhofer Institute for Solar Energy Systems]] under [[Adolf Goetzberger]]. In 1986 he moved to the Max Planck Institute for Solid State Research in Stuttgart, where he received his doctorate from the [[University of Stuttgart]] in 1988 under [[Hans-Joachim Queisser]], with work on ultrafast spectroscopy of semiconductors.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Leo |first=Karl |date=1988 |title=Untersuchung der Ultrakurzzeit-Dynamik von heißen Ladungsträgern in GaAs |journal=Doktorarbeit, Universität Stuttgart.}}</ref>
  
From 1989 to 1991 Leo was an [[Otto Hahn]] fellow and postdoctoral researcher at [[Bell Labs|AT&T Bell Laboratories]] in Holmdel, New Jersey. He then joined [[RWTH Aachen University|RWTH Aachen]] as an assistant professor and completed his habilitation in 1993.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Leo |first=Karl |date=1993 |title=Optische und elektronische Eigenschaften von Halbleiter-Übergittern und organischen Dünnschichten |journal=Habilitationsschrift, RWTH Aachen.}}</ref> Since the 1993/94 winter term he has held a full professorship for [[optoelectronics]] at the Dresden Integrated Center for Applied Physics and Photonic Materials (IAPP) of [[TU Dresden]], which he has headed (with an interruption from 2003 to 2006). In parallel he worked for the [[Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft|Fraunhofer Society]] from 2001 to 2013, first as a department head at the Fraunhofer Institute for Photonic Microsystems (IPMS)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Willkommen - Fraunhofer IPMS - Fraunhofer IPMS |url=https://www.ipms.fraunhofer.de/de.html |access-date=2026-07-20 |website=www.ipms.fraunhofer.de |language=de}}</ref> and, from 2008, as director of its organic-electronics division, which became Fraunhofer COMEDD in 2012. He has also held visiting professorships at [[Tohoku University]] (2009) and at King Abdullah University of Science and [[Technology]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=KAUST {{!}} A top research university in the Middle East |url=https://www.kaust.edu.sa/ |access-date=2026-07-20 |website=KAUST |language=en}}</ref> (KAUST, 2013–2014).

==Research focus==
Leo works in [[Semiconductor optical gain|semiconductor optics]] and the physics of thin organic films. In 1992 he achieved the first generation and detection of [[Bloch oscillation|Bloch oscillations]] in a semiconductor superlattice, an effect long considered impossible to observe.<ref name=":0" /> Much of his later work concerns the controlled electrical doping of organic semiconductors, which enabled p–i–n device architectures and organic light-emitting diodes with very low operating voltages and record power efficiencies; in 2009 his group reported a white OLED reaching the luminous efficiency of a fluorescent tube.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Reineke |first=Sebastian |last2=Lindner |first2=Frank |last3=Schwartz |first3=Gregor |last4=Seidler |first4=Nico |last5=Walzer |first5=Karsten |last6=Lüssem |first6=Björn |last7=Leo |first7=Karl |date=2009 |title=White organic light-emitting diodes with fluorescent tube efficiency |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nature08003 |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=459 |issue=7244 |pages=234–238 |doi=10.1038/nature08003 |issn=0028-0836|url-access=subscription }}</ref> His work on organic solar cells produced some of the highest reported efficiencies, later commercialised through the spin-off [[Heliatek]]. Further topics include organic permeable-base transistors, near-infrared organic photodetectors and organic bioelectronics. Leo has published more than 700 peer-reviewed papers and is co-inventor of around 60 patent families.
